title: CHARACTER & INTEGRITY: THE HIDDEN STRENGTH BEHIND WISDOM

sense.text: “A false balance is abomination to the Lord: but a just weight is his delight.” A false balance is falsifying something, and that is not good character. Whoever deals with a false balance is not acting right, and it is an abomination to the Lord. Integrity deals justly.

“The integrity of the upright shall guide them”. The upright is the one keeping the commandments, practicing what he preaches. His integrity guides him into doing the right thing no matter the circumstances. Without integrity, emotions guide you; lust guides you if you are not disciplined; pride, anger and impulse guide you. Integrity keeps you grounded.

Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles, aligning your actions with your values consistently, whether anyone is watching or not. It is an action, what you do over and over again. Character is the sum of your moral habits and values, your representation, what you are made of; integrity is the action behind it, the unwavering consistency of acting in line with those values, especially when it is difficult: when you get corrected, when it is not convenient, when your back is against the wall. You cannot be a damn hypocrite. You have to practice what you preach.

That integrity is what separates Israel from the nations, because it goes into the laws of the Most High. The nations live by primal instinct and do what they want; the laws of God build the discipline that says, I can't just do what I want to do. The Most High has been trying to teach us integrity since creation, and the Christian church is fighting against it. The other nations show they have no ethics and no sympathy: a man who can kill and go right to dinner with no remorse, who can roast a man alive or bash a baby's head against a stone, lacks what the Lord gave us. Esau is not upright; something is wrong with Esau. That is why Israel had to rule the nations, to give the world the example of morals and ethics, and without us in power the world is in shambles.

“but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.” The perverse one who lacks integrity and character will be destroyed by it.

“What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?” That is the scary mindset of convincing yourself that grace covers everything, and it is a terrible mindset to have.

It is the mindset of Christianity: I found grace, grace covers me, I can do what I want when I want; all I have to do is believe in Jesus, I don't have to do anything he says, just believe he is my Lord and saviour. Christianity is evil.

When temptation hits you alone online late at night and nobody from the congregation would know, integrity is to cut it off immediately and fight the temptation, not to entertain it privately, watch a little and justify it later, or tell yourself grace covers everything. The real battlefield is private: many fall spiritually in secret long before they fall publicly. The representative shows up at the Sabbath, saluting hard and bowing all the way down, but the real you shows up at home. The brother who comes in righteous and goes home and verbally, financially or physically abuses his wife, and the sister who bows to the floor here and goes home and cusses her husband out, keeps a filthy house, doesn't cook, lack integrity and have terrible, poor character.

“Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.” Everybody is going to be accounted for the works that they do. Period.

The works you choose to do are dictated by the integrity and character you have. That is how you make your decisions, how you deal with somebody in counsel, how you deal with your brother and sister.

precepts.why:
“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” A child is known by his doings, and by the Lord actions are weighed. Integrity is the action behind your character.

Your actions show who you are and what you are, and we are going to be judged by what we do: our actions, our works, whichever word you use. All of this is about action. You have to prove yourself to the Lord, constantly growing and constantly consistent, building your integrity and your character, even accounting for the bad actions we do.

We are the representation of this truth. When the world looks at the Israelites, they look at the brothers in the purple and gold, Israel United in Christ, because our leadership is heavy on integrity, character, structure and order: things Negroes never talked about, never had and never saw growing up. We have to be taught these traits, and around men who have built great moral character through their integrity, with hundreds of years of experience in the scriptures and in warring against different spirits.

sense.text: “Lord, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? who shall dwell in thy holy hill?” Our actions are weighed: the things we do, the works. We have to take account for all of them, even the bad actions we do, and the psalm answers who shall dwell in his holy hill by what a man does.

“He that walketh uprightly, and worketh righteousness”. Worketh is an action: putting your hand to the plow. That is what you are doing.

“and speaketh the truth in his heart.” He is the same all the time. He has moral and ethical traits that show he speaks with his heart correctly and honestly; he shows the integrity he has put behind his thoughts and how he deals with situations.

“He that backbiteth not with his tongue, nor doeth evil to his neighbour”. A man working toward righteousness and being upright is not going to do evil to his neighbour, because he has great moral character.

Many brothers and sisters like yes-men and yes-women, because that gives them the chance of murmuring and backbiting. The man working righteousness does not backbite and does not go and be vile against his neighbour. Many are putting no action into it, and they lack integrity.

“he honoureth them that fear the Lord.” “He that doeth these things shall never be moved.” We have to constantly be upright and working toward righteousness, and when we are put in those positions, think and use better judgment and discernment.

That comes with consistency, and with the company you keep. If you are the smartest person in the room, you are in the wrong room. Be around men you can learn from, men who will tell you, no, that ain't right, I wouldn't do that: men who will show you where you are in error.

“Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof is brutish.” Pride hates correction, but wisdom loves instruction. Being corrected is a good thing; that is how you grow.

When a brother corrects you and you feel embarrassed, wisdom is to examine yourself honestly, not to get defensive immediately, talk about him afterward behind his back as if he was out of the spirit, or leave emotionally. A strong character can handle correction without collapsing emotionally, because he has the morals and ethics to deal with it. The answer looks easy on paper; the problem is when it actually happens in real time. Many shut down or explode, overly emotional, because they got corrected. And Negro, you was wrong, and you know you was wrong. How can you fix something if you are not corrected?

Many do not like being around leadership because they will get stood up and asked questions, to see where their biblical knowledge, their moral knowledge and their integrity are. The elders and bishops are trying to build real, strong, righteous men, and you have to get corrected, because many of us lack these abilities. Whoever loves instruction keeps gaining knowledge, wisdom and understanding.

precepts.why: “Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die.” The man who hates reproof is brutish in Proverbs 12, and here he shall die.

“He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul”. In chapter 12 the one who loves instruction keeps gaining knowledge, wisdom and understanding. This one does not want to hear instruction or be corrected. He is always right, but wrong as hell.

He is not hurting somebody else; he is destroying his own soul, because he cannot be corrected, and that means he cannot grow. That is why a man can be here ten or fifteen years and still be a soldier, or an officer of ten: he knows everything else, but not why he has not grown.

“A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool.” A foolish man cannot allow wisdom to enter in. He sits in the school around these men for ten or fifteen years and sees everybody growing around him, but the wisdom cannot take hold and exalt him the way it exalts those who take hold of it, because he does not want it; he is fighting against it.

That is when it is time to take stock of yourself, and many do not want to, because they do not want the integrity that comes with the Bible.

sense.text: “Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom.” This is exactly the point: works are actions. That is great moral character. Wisdom shows up in your character, your discipline, your honesty, your consistency, and how you move when nobody is watching; a brother's wisdom and discernment show in how he deals with people, with his wife and children, and when he gets corrected.

“But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth.” The Lord did not put the spirit of strife and envy against one another in us. People pick up these traits and they become their moral character. That is why their name is always in some ish: the sister whose name always comes up, the brother always dropping the ball on his task. If that hits home and some are mad, I don't give a damn. It is what it is. Many answered the questions at the Marriage is Honorable politically correct rather than honestly. The one sister who answered honestly, even though it was not the right answer, can be dealt with and can grow; the politically correct answer hides where you really are.

“This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish. For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” These are not the characteristics we want associated with us. That wisdom did not come from the Lord; it was picked up through life in the world.

That is why we have to be around men who have been through these things and can teach us to be better men, better leaders, better husbands and better fathers. If you are not around such people, how can you learn these moral and ethical traits, work in integrity and build your character? Couples who came back from the Marriage is Honorable must keep the same energy and not backtrack to the negative; that would be not upholding their integrity.

“If thou desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord shall give her unto thee.” Keeping the commandments is an action. It is our foundation, how we live, the integrity we roll by.

When you are keeping the commandments, willfully and really keeping them, you have no choice but to have good integrity, and a man with good integrity has good character. You cannot keep the commandments with all your heart and all your soul and have horrible character. It makes no sense.
“For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction”. Our integrity and our moral character are directly tied to our fear toward God; they are one and the same.

precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is a crown of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish; both which are the gifts of God: and it enlargeth their rejoicing that love him. Wisdom raineth down skill and knowledge of understanding, and exalteth them to honour that hold her fast. The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and the branches thereof are long life.”

“The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord”: fearing God is the root of wisdom.

“The fear of the Lord driveth away sins”. A man who fears God keeps the commandments and upholds the integrity to do the right thing, and that is what drives the sin away. Whatever situation or inconvenience he is in, he keeps upholding the integrity of the commandments, because he works it over and over again.

“A wise man will fear in every thing”. That is integrity guiding you in every step: asking, is this the right move, is this in alignment with the laws of God?

“and in the day of sinning he will beware of offence”, because he is examining himself; he has the fear of God in him and walks in his integrity. “but a fool will not observe time.”

Not being able to take correction from the leadership, to digest it, understand it and receive it, is a sign of where your faith and belief are. We have to make sure we are walking in the fear of the Lord.

“The integrity of the upright shall guide them”. It goes with what Ecclesiasticus 18 just said: the wise man fears in everything and is wary of offence in the day of sinning. Your integrity guides you into doing the right thing and puts you in position.
